case_name: State of U.P. v Rasid and others
facts: The respondents herein and two others were charged for offences punishable under Sections 148, 452, 302 read with 149 and 307 IPC for having committed the murder of one Nasir Ahmad son of Mohd. Siddiq, his wife Chheddan and his two years old son Ishtiyak in the house of Mohd. Siddiq (PW-2) and for causing grievous and other injuries to PW-2 Mohd. Siddiq, PW-3 Mukhtar Ahmad, Nasir Ahmad PW-11 and another by name Masroor.

The prosecution case, in brief, is : these respondents along with 2 other acquitted accused persons formed themselves into an unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapons like rifles, countrymade pistols, Gandasas and lathis went to the house of PW-2 on 20.2.1982 at about 9.30 a.m.

The further case of the prosecution is that after the accused persons left, PW-2 left the place of the incident with a view to lodge a Police complaint and on the way while passing through the colony of Hargaon he met one Liyaqat (not examined) and told him about the incident and requested him to write down a complaint which was done by said Liyaqat on which PW-2 put his thumb impression.

The further case of the prosecution is that when PW-2 was being treated in the said hospital, the other wounded persons like PWs.3 and 11 along with child Ishtiyak were brought to the hospital by another Constable and were examined by the doctor.
issues: What was the time of occurrence?
Was the prosecution able to prove the involvement of the accused persons in the crime?
Can the evidence of the prosecution witnesses be relied upon to base a conviction?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution had relied upon the oral evidence of the eye witnesses coupled with the time of registering the complaint and the treatment given to the injured persons as also the opinion of the doctor who conducted the post mortem.
The prosecution had examined PWs.2, 3, 4, 11 and 12 as eye-witnesses to the occurrence.
respondent_arguments: The defence was contending that the incident in question must have occurred before the day break and there being no occasion to identify the assailants the accused persons were falsely implicated because of prior enmity.
The defence argued that the evidence of PW-4 Masoom Ali in regard to identification of the accused cannot be believed because he was not familiar with any of the accused.
court_reasoning: The learned Sessions Judge held that the prosecution had relied upon the oral evidence of the eye witnesses coupled with the time of registering the complaint and the treatment given to the injured persons as also the opinion of the doctor who conducted the post mortem.
The court came to the conclusion that a conviction could be safely based on the evidence of prosecution witnesses especially that of PW-2 with the aid of S. 149 IPC.
holding: The learned Sessions Judge acquitted accused No.6 Sadaqat and A-7 Liyaqat giving them the benefit of doubt and convicted other 15 persons for various offences punishable u/ss. 302 read with Sections 149, 452, 307 read with 149 IPC.
The High Court allowed the appeal and set aside the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants.
